values.Question: How do I activate a private or public preview feature for specific customers in the Release Manager UI?
values.Answer: Every feature has a **Releases tab regardless of its stage**, and any customer can be activated from that tab — there is no separate private/public-preview screen. Two prerequisites catch people out: the feature must be **scheduled into a release** (if its release is `N/A` nothing works), and the workspace must already be **assigned to a cohort**. QA example given: `https://admin.tcpqa.com/platform/release-manager/products/360/features/8/details`.
values.Source: Kyle Hall, with Grant Maines and Paul Covington confirming by testing — AR channel, 2026-08-25/26
values.Promote when: Blueprint documents pre-release activation in the UI; the docs currently only cover the API endpoint.

values.Question: Why are there no workspaces listed when I try to activate a feature?
values.Answer: **Because none of the product's workspaces are assigned to a cohort.** Features can only be enabled for workspaces that have a cohort assignment; if none are assigned the activation list comes back empty rather than telling you why. The same symptom appears when the feature itself is not scheduled into a release. Fix either and the workspaces appear on the feature's **Feature activations** tab, where you can multi-select and use **Activate feature**, or open a single workspace row and use the **Active** slider.
values.Source: Grant Maines (determined by testing), corroborated by Paul Covington's own resolution — AR channel, 2026-08-25/26
values.Promote when: Release Manager surfaces an explanatory empty state, at which point this entry can be dropped.
values.Reviewer notes: PROVISIONAL — confirm before publishing. Grant Maines worked this out by testing, not from the AR team. Confirm the empty-list cause with Kyle Hall or Jay McCormick before publishing — the fix is a one-line answer and getting it wrong sends people hunting the wrong setting.

values.Question: How do I delete a feature in Release Manager?
values.Answer: **Only while editing it.** Open the feature for edit and there is a **Delete** button at the bottom of the edit dialog — there is no delete action in the feature list. Deletion is expected to be blocked once a feature has been enabled for a workspace, and there may be other guard rules.

values.Question: Are workspaces assigned to a default cohort automatically when a product is licensed?
values.Answer:
**No — nothing is assigned by default.** Automatic default assignment is the long-term direction but is not how it works today: AR moved to an **opt-in model for the 2027 rollout**. Someone in the product's PM/PO group must assign participating product workspaces to a cohort, either in **Release Manager — which supports bulk cohort assignment** — or through the AR API. You do not have to assign workspaces one at a time.

**Timing guidance:** per what FACC was told on 2026-08-25, **wait until after the November dry run** to make cohort assignments, so AR emails and notifications are not triggered inadvertently.

values.Source: Nate Hanna, AR channel 2026-08-31, answering Mathew Hanson

Hanna now says Release Manager itself supports bulk cohort assignment. Reconcile those two sentences rather than adding a second entry. The 'no default assignment' and 'wait until after the November dry run' points are genuinely new.

values.Question: Do Aligned Releases emails go out in the CI and QA environments, or only in production?
values.Answer:
**They go out in all environments.** This was checked directly: AR is currently sending emails in every environment, including `tcpci.com` and `tcpqa.com`, not just `tylerportico.com`. The platform team deliberately replicates functionality across `tcpci.com → tcpqa.com → tylerportico.com` because code moves through each environment in turn; per-environment feature flags exist but are only used when absolutely necessary.

**Why this matters:** AR notifications go to the **Client System (Org) Administrators** of the selected organization/workspace. So a test activation in QA or CI can email real people. Treat AR testing in any environment as capable of sending live mail, and choose the org and workspace accordingly.
values.Source: Kyle Hall, 2026-08-31, after verifying (question raised by Paul Covington); environment model described by Vijay Venkataraman and the testing implication by Nate Hanna, 2026-08-28
values.Promote when: Blueprint documents AR notification behaviour per environment. Re-check if AR ever adds an environment-level email suppression flag.

values.Question: Which organizations should I avoid selecting when testing AR notifications?
values.Answer:
**Avoid the shared internal orgs** — `demo`, `test`, `dev`, `uat`, `impl`, `train`, `testinprod` and similar. They contain large numbers of Tyler staff holding Org Admin permissions, and AR notifications go to Org Admins, so activating a feature against one of them mails everybody in it.

**Do this instead:** have an internal org created specifically for your product's testing, and select that. Ask the OneTyler team (Vijay Venkataraman) to provision one.
values.Source: Vijay Venkataraman, AR channel 2026-08-28
values.Promote when: a documented list of test-safe orgs exists.

values.Question: Can I mark my product's release as dependent on another product's release, so they stay in the same cohort?
values.Answer:
**No. AR does not manage product dependencies.** It tracks and communicates release information and feature relationships; it does not coordinate release sequencing or cohort alignment across products.

What AR does offer is **feature cross-referencing**: products can reference each other's features to represent a shared capability across the portfolio, which gives traceability and visibility into how those features are used. It does not enforce anything.

AR's operating principle is that **products deploy and release features independently**. Participating teams should not assume another product will release a feature at the same time, and should design integrations accordingly. Planning, integration and release readiness stay with the teams; Business Units get the cross-product analysis view for their own planning.
values.Source: Nate Hanna, AR channel 2026-06-17, answering Kevin Baker's question about 'CM 2027.1 requires 2027.1 MJ'

values.Question: Our product depends on a shared platform product (e.g. Content Manager) that is not in Aligned Releases yet. Do we have to defer our own participation?
values.Answer: **No.** Dependent products do not need to defer AR participation until the shared platform product comes online. Communicate the platform product's capabilities within **your own feature catalog as an embedded capability** — the same way you would treat a third-party plugin or an integrated service. As shared platform products onboard to AR in later quarters, that changes.
values.Source: Nate Hanna, FACC channel 2026-07-02, promised follow-up from the 2026-06-30 FACC meeting

values.Question: Our mobile app cannot guarantee an App Store or Play Store approval date. How do we meet the Aligned Releases requirements?
values.Answer:
**Feature activation cannot depend on code deployment** — that is the AR principle that resolves this. Shipping the mobile binary and activating an impactful feature are separate concerns.

So: mobile teams **release app versions throughout the quarter** as store dynamics require, and **gate impactful functionality behind feature flags** until the appropriate AR activation window. The store approval timeline stops being an AR problem because the feature is not live until you activate it.

A practical tip from a team already doing this: submit to the store **weeks ahead** and use the store's own scheduled-release date to align the binary's availability, so a rejection has slack to be fixed. App Store submission and release can be scheduled separately.
values.Source: Nate Hanna (the AR principle), 2026-07-14 and 2026-06-19; Nathan Westfall (the submit-early practice), 2026-07-14 — FACC channel, raised by Kevin Baker for Workforce Mobile and My Civic
values.Promote when: the AR guidance page on mobile deployment is published outside Coda.

values.Question: How far into the future does Aligned Releases create release objects?
values.Answer: **At least a rolling year out**, and it can go further if that is useful — release details are known indefinitely, so the horizon is a choice rather than a limit.
values.Source: Kyle Hall, AR channel 2026-05-28, answering Cedar Cranson

values.Question: Can I revert a release cohort that has been marked as released, so I can reuse it for testing?
values.Answer:
**There is no revert.** Two things follow from that:

- **You can re-run the execute endpoint.** Calling it again on the same release cohort is supported and updates the **Executed** date, which is usually enough to re-test.
- **You cannot just make new ones.** Creating a `ReleaseCohort` is a restricted action, so spinning up a fresh cohort per test run is not available to product teams.

A project to make AR testing easier — create a test release and release cohort tied to your product, then tear it all down afterwards — was upcoming as of 2026-05-14. Check whether it has landed before repeating the 'no revert' answer.
values.Source: Matt Bartel, AR channel 2026-05-14, answering John Jenusaitis
values.Promote when: the AR testing-support project ships — this entry then needs rewriting, not just re-confirming.

values.Question: Is releaseCohortId the same as the cohort number 1–4?
values.Answer:
**No.** The cohort number is 1–4; `releaseCohortId` is the identifier of the **link between a cohort and a release**, so it differs per release.

To mark a product released using `/api/v1/execute/by-releasecohort/{releaseCohortId}/product/{productRegistrationId}` you need two calls: get the release cohorts to obtain the id, then mark released.

**Easier route:** a newer endpoint takes the release id instead and resolves the release cohort itself —

```
POST v1/release/:releaseId/product/:productRegistrationId/product-releases
```

Put `cohorts: [<cohort number>]` in the request body and it works out the right release cohort id from the release id and the cohort number. This was pushed ahead of the docs, so it may not appear in the published API reference.
values.Source: Matt Bartel, AR channel 2026-05-11 and 2026-05-14, answering John Jenusaitis
values.Promote when: the `product-releases` endpoint appears in the Blueprint AR API reference — then point at the docs instead.

values.Question: The features and products arrays come back empty on the release-cohort response. Does that mean nothing is assigned?
values.Answer:
**No — they are always empty there.** The release-cohort endpoint re-uses the release object, and those collections are never populated on that load, so an empty array tells you nothing about what is assigned or released. It is a known source of confusion and the object may be changed.

Use the dedicated endpoints instead:

```
v1/release/{id}/features
v1/release/{id}/products
```
values.Source: Matt Bartel, AR channel 2026-05-11/12, answering John Jenusaitis
values.Promote when: the release-cohort response stops carrying the unused collections.

values.Question: Can I query cohort assignments filtered by cohort, rather than pulling every workspace for a product and filtering client-side?
values.Answer:
**Yes — there is a `cohorts` query parameter.** It was added to the cohort-assignment endpoint and the AR SDK was updated to match, so you no longer have to fetch `/api/v1/cohort-assignment/product/<product>` in full and filter in your own code. Filtering by **workspace** and **org** was being added in the same pass.

The change went to `tcpci` first, so confirm it has reached the environment you are calling.
values.Source: Matt Bartel, AR channel 2026-05-11, answering John Jenusaitis (working on feeding AR cohorts into an FME segment)
values.Promote when: the `cohorts`, `workspace` and `org` filters are in the Blueprint AR API reference.

values.Question: Is the client release-notes email four weeks before Cohort 1, or four weeks before Cohort 4 / GA?
values.Answer: **Four weeks before the start of the GA activation window — i.e. four weeks before the Cohort 1 date.** The Aligned Releases system sends this communication; individual business units are **not** expected to send it separately.
